  COVID-19 PUBLIC PARTICIPATION OPTIONS
Due to the existing COVID-19 health emergency and the social distancing measures currently in effect, and pursuant
to Assembly Bill 361, please note that members of the public will be allowed only to observe and address the City
Council Meeting of Tuesday, February 8, 2022, at 2:00 p.m. (or 1:00 p.m. if Closed Session) by telephone,
video and other electronic means, as follows:

  1. Written Public Comments: Members of the public may choose to submit comments electronically for
  consideration by the Inglewood City Council/Successor Agency/Housing Authority/Finance Authority/Parking
  Authority/Joint Powers Authority (Legislative Body) by sending them to the City Clerk/Secretary at
  athompson@cityofinglewood.org, and Deputy City Clerk at aallen@cityofinglewood.org. To ensure
  distribution to the members of the Legislative Body prior to consideration of the agenda, please submit
  comments prior to 8:00 a.m. the day of the meeting, and in the body of the email, please identify the agenda
  number or subject matter. Correspondence should indicate the meeting date and agenda item. Comments
  received after 8:00 a.m. and prior to the close of the public hearings will be made part of the official public
  record of the meeting. Contact the Office of the City Clerk at 310-412-5280 with any questions.

Inglewood, California
  February 8, 2022

The City Council of the City of Inglewood, California held a regular meeting on Tuesday,
February 8, 2022, in the Council Chambers in City Hall of said City.

Mayor Butts called the City Council into Closed Session at the hour of 1:02 p.m.
The City Clerk announced the presence of a quorum as follows:
  Present:  Mayor Butts, Council Members Dotson, Padilla, Morales,
  Faulk; and
  Absent:  None.
City officials and personnel present for closed session were as follows:

  Aisha L. Thompson  City Clerk
  Artie Fields  City Manager
  Ken Campos  City Attorney
  Angela Allen  Deputy City Clerk

PUBLIC COMMENTS REGARDING CLOSED SESSION ITEMS. Mayor Butts
inquired if there were any persons present who wished to address the City Council on
Closed Session Item Nos. CS-1, CS-2, and CS-3.

There was no response.

Mayor Butts recessed the City Council at the hour of 1:02 p.m. for Closed Session Item
Nos. CS-1, CS-2, and CS-3.

  *****************

Following the Pledge of Allegiance to the flag of our Country, Mayor Butts called the
City Council into joint session with the Successor Agency, and Housing Authority, at the
hour of 2:01 p.m.
The City Clerk/Successor Agency Secretary/Housing Authority Secretary/ announced the
presence of a quorum as follows:

  Present:  Mayor/Successor Agency Chairman/Housing Authority
  Chairman Butts, Council Members/Successor Agency
  Members/Housing Authority Members Dotson, Padilla,
  Morales, and Faulk; and
  Absent:  None.

City/Successor Agency / Housing Authority officials and personnel present were as
follows:
  Aisha L. Thompson  City Clerk/Secretary*
  Artie Fields  City Manager/Executive Director*
  Ken Campos  City Attorney/General Counsel*
  Louis Atwell  Assistant City Manager/Public Works Director
  Angela Allen  Deputy City Clerk

*Serves as indicated for the Successor Agency, and Housing Authority.

PUBLIC COMMENTS – AGENDA ITEMS.  Mayor/Successor Agency
Chairman/Housing Authority Chairman Butts inquired if there were any persons present
who wished to address the City Council/Successor Agency/Housing Authority on any
item on the Agendas.

Vandalena Mahoney spoke concerning a matter not on the Agenda, and was advised to
call back towards the end of the meeting to address her concerns.
   February 8, 2022

142.9  PAYMENT OF WARRANTS AND BILLS. It was moved by Council Member
  /Successor Agency Member / Housing Authority Member Morales, and seconded by
  Council Member /Successor Agency Member / Housing Authority Member Faulk that
  the demands presented to the City Council/Successor Agency/Housing Authority dated
  February 3, 2022, in the amount of $1,241,727.36, are hereby allowed, and the City
  Clerk/Successor Agency Secretary/Housing Authority Secretary is hereby authorized to
  certify upon said registers that said demands are so approved. The motion was carried by
  the following roll call vote:
  Ayes: Council Members/Successor Agency Members/Housing Authority Members
  Dotson, Padilla, Morales, Faulk, and Mayor/Successor Agency
  Chairman/Housing Authority Chairman Butts; and
  Noes: None.

 125  RESOLUTION NO. 22-50 ADOPTED - AUTHORIZING THE CITY TO
  IMPLEMENT TELECONFERNCE PUBLIC MEETINGS FROM FEBRUARY 8,
  2022, THROUGH MARCH 10, 2022, PURSUANT TO ASSEMBLY BILL 361.
  Staff report dated February 8, 2022, was presented recommending adoption of a
  resolution authorizing the City Council, and all other legislative bodies of the City, to
  continue to conduct public meetings via teleconference from February 8, 2022, through
  March 10, 2022, pursuant to Assembly Bill 361.

  It was moved by Council Member Morales, and seconded by Council Member Dotson
  that Resolution No. 22-50 entitled:

  A RESOLUTION OF THE CITY COUNCIL OF THE CITY OF
  INGLEWOOD, CALIFORNIA AUTHORIZING THE CITY
  COUNCIL AND ALL OTHER LEGISLATIVE BODIES TO
  CONTINUTE TO CONDUCT PUBLIC MEETINGS VIA
  TELECONFERENCE FROM FEBRUARY 8, 2022, THROUGH
  MARCH 10, 2022, PURSUANT TO AB 361.

  be adopted. The motion was carried by the following roll call vote:
  Ayes: Council Members Dotson, Padilla, Morales, Faulk, and Mayor Butts; and
  Noes: None.

126  MINUTES. It was moved by Council Member Morales, and seconded by Council
  Member Padilla that the Minutes for the City Council Meetings held on January 4, 2022,
  and January 11, 2022, be approved. The motion was carried by the following roll call
  vote:
  Ayes: Council Members Dotson, Padilla, Morales, Faulk, and Mayor Butts; and
  Noes: None

132  CLAIMS DENIED. Letters from the Office of the City Attorney recommending the
  following:
  A. Reject Claims Pursuant to Government Code, Section 913:
  1. Chalondrea R. Bates for alleged personal injury; restroom floor dangerous condition
  on August 12, 2021.
  2. Frank Pelletier for alleged vehicle damage; pothole on January 7, 2022.

  It was moved by Council Member Morales, and seconded by Council Member Padilla
  that the City Council does hereby Reject Claims listed as A-1 and A-2. The motion was
  carried by the following roll call vote:
  Ayes: Council Members Dotson, Padilla, Morales, Faulk, and Mayor Butts; and
  Noes: None.

125  PAYMENT AUTHORIZED – CAUVEL & DACEY, P.C. Staff report dated February
  8, 2022, was presented recommending authorization of payment of an outstanding
  invoice submitted by Cauvel & Dacey, P.C., for legal services rendered for the
  construction of the Emergency Operations Center.

  2
   February 8, 2022

  It was moved by Council Member Morales, and seconded by Council Member Padilla
  that the City Council does hereby approve authorize payment in the amount of $17,050.
  The motion was carried by the following roll call vote:
  Ayes: Council Members Dotson, Padilla, Morales, Faulk, and Mayor Butts; and
  Noes: None.

142  AGREEMENT NO. 22-141 APPROVED – LANCE, SOLL & LUNGHARD, LLP.
  Staff report dated February 8, 2022, was presented recommending approval of a three
  (3)-year agreement (with an option to renew an additional two (2) years in one (1)-year
  increments) with Lance, Soll & Lunghard, LLP, for Professional Audit Services for the
  City of Inglewood, per Request for Proposal (RFP) No. 0172.

  It was moved by Council Member Morales, and seconded by Council Member Padilla
  that the City Council does hereby approve Agreement No. 22-141, in a total amount not
  to exceed $353,833. The motion was carried by the following roll call vote:
  Ayes: Council Members Dotson, Padilla, Morales, Faulk, and Mayor Butts; and
  Noes: None.

171  PAYMENT AUTHORIZED – HANNIBAL MEDIA GROUP (HMG). Staff report
  dated February 8, 2022, was presented recommending authorization of payment of
  invoices submitted by Hannibal Media Group (HMG), for services rendered during
  planning for the City’s 39th Annual King Day Celebration.

  It was moved by Council Member Morales, and seconded by Council Member Padilla
  that the City Council does hereby authorize payment in the amount of $8,000. The
  motion was carried by the following roll call vote:
  Ayes: Council Members Dotson, Padilla, Morales, Faulk, and Mayor Butts; and
  Noes: None.

301  AGREEMENT NO. 22-142 APPROVED – MOTIVE GROUP, INC.;
  CATEGORICAL EXEMPTION AFFIRMED - IN COMPLIANCE WITH
  CALIFORNIA ENVIRONMENTAL QUALITY ACT (CEQA). Staff report dated
  February 8, 2022, was presented recommending approval of an agreement with Motive
  Group, Inc. representing Pepsi Cola Advertising and Marketing, Inc.

  It was moved by Council Member Morales, and seconded by Council Member Faulk that
  the City Council does hereby: 1) Approve Agreement No. 22-142; and 2) Affirm a
  categorical exemption (CE) in compliance with the California Environmental Quality Act
  (CEQA). The motion was carried by the following roll call vote:
  Ayes: Council Members Dotson, Padilla, Morales, Faulk, and Mayor Butts; and
  Noes: None.

132.6  CLOSED  SESSION  –  ANTICIPATED  LITIGATION;  WORKERS’
  COMPENSATION CLAIM OF MARGARITA CRUZ: CLAIM NUMBERS 14-
  119466 AND 14-120189. Closed session – Confidential – Attorney/Client Privilege; City
  Council Conference with Legal Counsel – Anticipated Litigation Pursuant to Government
  Code Section 54956.9(d)(2); Workers’ Compensation Claim of Margarita Cruz: Claim
  Numbers 14-119466 and 14-120189.

  It was moved by Council Member Morales, and seconded by Council Member Faulk that
  the City Council does hereby approve settlement. The motion was carried by the
  following roll call vote:
  Ayes: Council Members Dotson, Padilla, Morales, Faulk, and Mayor Butts; and
  Noes: None.

  3
   February 8, 2022

132.6  CLOSED  SESSION  –  ANTICIPATED  LITIGATION;  WORKERS’
  COMPENSATION CLAIM OF NICOLE LOUDERMILK; CLAIM NUMBER 19-
  142683. Closed Session – Confidential – Attorney/Client Privilege; City Council
  Conference with Legal Counsel – Anticipated Litigation Pursuant to Government Code
  Section 54956.9(d)(2); Workers’ Compensation Claim of Nicole Loudermilk: Claim
  Number 19-142683.

  Status Given; Direction Given to Staff.

132.6  CLOSED  SESSION  –  ANTICIPATED  LITIGATION;  WORKERS’
  COMPENSATION CLAIM OF CLYDEAN PINSON; CLAIM NUMBER 19-
  140916. Closed Session – Confidential – Attorney/Client Privilege; City Council
  Conference with Legal Counsel – Anticipated Litigation Pursuant to Government Code
  Section 54956.9(d)(2); Workers’ Compensation Claim of Clydean Pinson: Claim Number
  19-140916.

  It was moved by Council Member Morales, and seconded by Council Member Faulk that
  the City Council does hereby approve settlement. The motion was carried by the
  following roll call vote:
  Ayes: Council Members Dotson, Padilla, Morales, Faulk, and Mayor Butts; and
  Noes: None.

126  REPORTS – CITY CLERK. The City Clerk, Aisha L. Thompson notified residents of
  the next scheduled Redistricting Public Hearing has been rescheduled for March 1, 2022,
  at the hour of 2:00 p.m. She paid homage to Shirley Chisholm for Black History Month,
  mentioning she was the first African American woman in Congress (1968) and the first
  woman and African American to seek the nomination for president of the United States
  from one of the two major political parties (1972). The City Clerk also wished Council
  Member Faulk a Happy Birthday.

  PUBLIC COMMENTS – AGENDA ITEMS. Mayor Butts inquired if there were any
  persons present who wished to address the City Council on any matter connected with
  City business not elsewhere on the Agenda.

  There was no response.

  There being no further business to be presented, Mayor Butts thanked the Inglewood
  Police Department, the City Council, Brian Walker, Crystal McGlover, and everyone in
  the Emergency Preparedness Department for doing a top-notch, and professional job on
  the Joint Operations Center, and declared the meeting adjourned, at the hour of 2:29 p.m.

  Approved this 1st day of March, 2022.

  _________________________
  Aisha L. Thompson, City Clerk

  ________________________
  James Butts, Jr., Mayor
